page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.4xlarge is a high-clock-speed computing instance powered by Intel Xeon 8369HB processors running at a base clock frequency of 3.3 GHz. Configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64 GB of memory, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Virtualization is handled via KVM with dedicated CPU core allocation. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 for accelerated vector computations, alongside hardware AES acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier execution across most standard workloads, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,380 and a PassMark CPU score of 18,076.58. The memory subsystem reflects higher throughput, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score of 2,769.96 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 88.47 GB/sec. CPU-based machine learning inference handles small models reasonably well at 985.84 prompt tokens per second, but degrades significantly when handling 7B parameter models, registering a weak 23.99 prompt tokens per second.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block devices and a 6 Gbps baseline network interface. This makes ecs.hfg7.4xlarge an efficient platform for mid-tier application architectures, Redis caching layers, web application serving, software compilation pipelines, and transactional database services that require steady clock frequencies without local storage persistence.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.4xlarge is a high-frequency compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring a 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM. Operating under KVM virtualization with dedicated core assignment, it features instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16. The instance includes no onboard local storage, depending on external storage volumes across a 6 Gbps baseline network interface, and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation indicates consistent mid-range performance, with multi-core scores reaching 8,380 in Geekbench and 18,076.58 in PassMark, accompanied by top-quartile PassMark memory throughput. The server provides balanced resource allocation without local storage overhead, making it suitable for transactional relational databases, software build runners, static and dynamic web serving, and memory-oriented caching workloads like Redis.
